newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end down after French left victory.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end down after French left victory.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mostly lower, languishing on fallout from a left-wing victory in French elections.

Marks initially firmed on the election news, but soon switched course. Traders zeroed in on worries that the Socialist win would improve the chances of Italy and Spain joining the euro and weaken the European currency.
Bundesbank board member Edgar Meister said overnight the French election may put European monetary and economic union (EMU) on course for "rougher waters."
June marks sank to the lowest price in more than a month.
The contract broke through support at the bottom of a four-week consolidation band and edged to the lowest price since the April 28 contract low.
With triple-bottom support at $0.5853 and $0.5852 gone, some technicians worried that June marks would have trouble finding technical footing.
The contract low lurks at $0.5768.
Late in the trading session, Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse said it would be wrong to soften EMU criteria to help Germany join the EMU, but futures registered scant impact to that statement.
He also said the Bonn government's plan to plug fiscal holes by revaluing reserves was "comparable to creative accounting."
The ongoing German asset revaluation dispute has further stoked worries of a broad-based and soft euro, traders said.
Swiss francs saw heavy volume and selling pressure in futures pits, traders said.
Several traders said the dollar was poised for gains and European currencies for losses as long as political and EMU turmoil continues in Europe.
"It's all pretty bearish Europe," an IMM trader said.
"Italy and Spain are going to create a weaker euro," noted one currency analyst. "And who emerges the leader in the Chirac-Kohl battle with Jospin remains to be seen," he said.
Socialist leader Lionel Jospin was appointed new prime minister by French President Jacques Chirac.
"How do you trade it? You stay out of the area for a while," he said.
That political friction could keep the dollar well supported, he said.
Trade was nervous and brisk in Canadian dollar futures Monday, awaiting results of Canada's general election.
June Canadian dollar futures ended up slightly, in the middle of their overnight and daily range.

At the close, yen was down $0.000031 at $0.008591, marks lost $0.0089 to $0.5783, Swiss franc eased $0.0100 to $0.6993, sterling fell $0.0062 to $1.6342, Can dollar rose $0.0009 to $0.7278, Aussie dollar lost $0.0021 to $0.7581, Mexican peso rose $0.000200 to $0.125625.
